simple.meaning: עָסַס (ʻâçaç) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to squeeze out juice ; figuratively, to trample.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 1 time in Malachi, beginning at Malachi 3:21. Its meaning becomes clearer as the uses are compared.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to עָסַס (H6072) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: עָסַס (ʻâçaç) / H6072 is traced through Malachi 3:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to squeeze out juice ; figuratively, to trample
definitions.full: H6072. asas [ עָסַס ] verb press, crush , by treading, tread down (Late Hebrew עֲסִיסִיה crushed wheat; compare Arabic go the rounds, [tramp], prowl ; Syriac explore , see Brock); — Qal Perfect 2masculine plural figurative וְעַסּוֺתֶם הָֽרְשָׁעִים Malachi 3:21 (consecutive).
